summary.text: Radiocarbon dating works out the age of objects containing organic material using radiocarbon, a radioactive isotope of carbon.
Half of a sample's radiocarbon decays in about 5,730 years, so the oldest dates it can reliably measure are around 50,000 years ago.
Its impact on archaeology is often called the "radiocarbon revolution", letting researchers date key transitions such as the end of the last ice age.

facts.label: Developed by
facts.value: Willard Libby, Nobel Prize in Chemistry 1960

facts.label: Ocean surface water
facts.value: Shows an apparent age of about 400 years

items.prompt: Gas made from petroleum is tested for radiocarbon and shows no radiocarbon activity at all. Why?

options.label: Petroleum never came from living things
It is so old its radiocarbon has gone
Gas cannot hold carbon atoms of any kind
Refining adds fresh carbon to the gas

items.explain: Methane created from petroleum showed no radiocarbon activity because of its age.

items.prompt: A seal that died last year is radiocarbon dated. What result would you expect?

options.label: An age of almost exactly one year
No result, since seals hold no carbon
An age in the future, below zero
An apparent age of hundreds of years

items.explain: Marine organisms such as shells and marine mammals like whales and seals have radiocarbon ages that appear to be hundreds of years old.

items.prompt: A sample picks up a small amount of very old carbon before testing. How does that change the result?

options.label: It looks older than it really is
It looks younger than it really is
It makes no difference to the date
It makes the sample impossible to test

items.explain: A sample contaminated with 1% old carbon will appear about 80 years older than it truly is, whatever its date.

items.prompt: How did Willard Libby and James Arnold check that radiocarbon dating actually worked?

options.label: They waited decades to watch a sample decay
They compared it with the depth of rock layers
They dated samples whose ages were already known
They counted tree rings in the same samples

items.explain: They tested the theory on samples of known age, such as samples from the tombs of two Egyptian kings, dated independently to 2625 BC ± 75 years.

items.prompt: After about 11,400 years, roughly how much of a sample's original radiocarbon is left?

options.label: About half
About an eighth
None at all
About a quarter

items.explain: Each half-life halves what remains: a quarter is left after 11,400 years and an eighth after 17,100 years.

items.prompt: Before radiocarbon dating, archaeologists struggled to compare sites on different continents. What did the method add?

options.label: A way to compare dates of events across great distances
A way to read written records left at each site
A way to date stone tools from the minerals inside them
A way to date sites without collecting any samples

items.explain: Besides more accurate dating within sites, radiocarbon dating allows comparison of dates of events across great distances.
